policy.authorization_rule: The complete macro body, claim ID, and manuscript section must exactly match authorized_tex and allowed_locations.
policy.artifact_rule: Quantitative table or figure claims require an authorized artifact ID, generated output, provenance sidecar, and manuscript binding.
policy.prose_rule: Claim-bearing quantitative, accuracy, validation, parity, and performance prose outside a registered macro or artifact is prohibited.
policy.screening_rule: A section admitted by a numerical-screening gate follows the campaign_macro_rule and additionally states the recorded outcome (accepted screening, preregistered null or recorded characterization) as recorded: a null is admitted under the frozen cusp/cell definitions only, is never phrased as an existence disproof, and lineage records (superseded or failed studies) appear only inside registered non-claims.
policy.working_tree_rule: Uncommitted scientific inputs are never evidence; paper-owned generated sources are hash-bound pending integration.
policy.campaign_macro_rule: A section admitted by a numerical-campaign gate may render numbers only through evidence macros whose value, artifact path, JSON pointer and SHA-256 are recorded in the campaign's evidence file and regenerated from the sealed bundle by the checker; the section may type no literal digit, and its claim-bearing sentences remain exact EvidenceClaim bodies bound to the campaign manifest.
policy.section_input_rule: Files bound through \input{sections/...} are flattened into the manuscript before every claim, citation and prose check; a section is not a way around the matrix.

claims.authorized_tex: A preregistered one-shot collisionless test-particle campaign of \WlfPooledTrials{} electron orbits in a qualified finite-element magnetostatic field is admitted as numerical evidence: it recorded \WlfPooledReflected{} reflections and a per-cell bimodal wall-hit pattern, and it is neither a self-consistent plasma calculation nor a thruster-performance result.

claims.authorized_tex: The run terminated in state \texttt{\WlfTerminalState} with \WlfGatesTrue{} of \WlfGateCount{} binding gates true and \WlfValidatorsPassed{} validator calls with \WlfValidatorsFailed{} failures; every case was re-integrated by the exact authority replay (\WlfReplayCount{} replays). Within the collisionless prescribed-field test-particle model classified as \texttt{\WlfClassification}, the wall-hit probability lies between \WlfWallPMin{} and \WlfWallPMax{} across the \WlfCaseCount{} preregistered cases with \texttt{\WlfIntervalMethod} intervals; pooled with equal weights over all \WlfPooledTrials{} orbits it is \WlfPooledWallP{} (interval [\WlfPooledWallLo, \WlfPooledWallHi]), with \WlfPooledEscape{} domain escapes (\WlfPooledEscapeP), exactly \WlfPooledReflected{} reflections and \WlfPooledIncomplete{} timeouts or numerical failures. The pooled value averages a bimodal per-cell result: the two interior cells lose every launch to the wall (\WlfCellTwoThreeWall{} of \WlfCellTwoThreeTrials), the exit cell beyond the dielectric end escapes entirely (\WlfCellFourEscape{} of \WlfCellFourTrials), and the injector-side cell depends on the launch direction (\WlfCellOneMinusWallP{} wall loss for launches toward the injector plane against \WlfCellOnePlusWallP, that is \WlfCellOnePlusWall{} of \WlfCellOnePlusTrials, toward the exit).
allowed_locations: Collisionless full-orbit electron wall loss in the divergent-exit field
claims.evidence_level_justification: The campaign is numerical evidence about a collisionless, prescribed-field, test-particle model of electron orbits in one qualified P2 magnetostatic field, verified at the code level (manufactured helix orders, CPU/CUDA parity, exact authority replay) and at the solution level (timestep refinement, field-map refinement and enlargement, exact energy gate, Wilson intervals). The framework's only mechanism for accepted numerical evidence is the one used for L0: a typed committed manifest, artifacts bound by Git blob and SHA-256 at a resolvable revision, exact registered claim text, and generated artifacts with provenance sidecars. That mechanism is applied here through the numerical-campaign gate GATE-WALL-LOSS-V4. The campaign is not a field-resolved reduced performance model (no L0 mapping; the coupling export is export-only), not a coupled hybrid plasma model, and neither particle-in-cell nor experimental, so it is recorded outside the L1--L3 ladder and opens none of those gates; its tier in the V&V protocol is verification, never validation.

claims.evidence_level_justification: The campaign is one accepted, preregistered, single-execution numerical campaign about a declared component model: the accepted L0 conservation model evaluated under the declared multiplicative cusp-survival closure CL-1 and declared uniform priors. That is the object the numerical-campaign gate kind was defined for (one accepted campaign on a declared component model), so the kind is reused through GATE-MDO-L0-V1 with the same mechanism as the wall-loss campaign: a typed committed manifest, artifacts bound by Git blob and SHA-256 at a resolvable revision, exact registered claim text, generated artifacts with provenance sidecars, and a campaign-specific checker. Its estimands are properties of the optimisers (hypervolume per budget, paired comparisons, seed variance, Pareto sizes) and of the declared evaluation chain (robust-versus-nominal fronts, sensitivity to the cusp prior); it is optimiser evidence, not performance evidence. It is not the L1 field-resolved reduction (no field solve, geometry variable or L0 mapping), not L2 (no plasma coupling; the corrected four-cell solver was probed and not used) and not L3, so it opens none of GATE-L1, GATE-L2 or GATE-L3, and it does not populate the F3-verified benchmark field of the committed campaign policy.

claims.authorized_tex: Pooled over the \MdoUniqueDesigns{} unique designs evaluated by all runs, the robust front holds \MdoRobustFront{} designs (hypervolume \MdoPooledRobustHv{} over \MdoRobustCandidates{} robust-feasible designs) and the nominal front, a re-evaluation of the same designs at the prior midpoints under the nominal constraint, holds \MdoNominalFront{} designs (hypervolume \MdoPooledNominalHv{} over \MdoNominalCandidates{} nominally feasible designs); the two fronts share \MdoSharedDesigns{} designs (Jaccard index \MdoJaccard) and \MdoNominalRobustFeasible{} of the \MdoNominalFront{} nominal-front designs are robust-feasible. The nominal front reaches an electrical-to-beam efficiency of \MdoNominalEffMax{} and a specific impulse of \MdoNominalIspMax{}~s, whereas the robust front reaches \MdoRobustEffMax{} and \MdoRobustIspMax{}~s, both over anode powers from \MdoRobustPowerMin{} to \MdoRobustPowerMax{}~W. The predeclared separability expectation held on the dense reference (largest relative spread of the robust-to-nominal objective ratio \MdoSeparabilitySpreadMax{} against a tolerance of \MdoSeparabilityTolerance; passed: \MdoSeparabilityPassed): under the declared closure the cusp probabilities rescale thrust, specific impulse and efficiency uniformly, so the two fronts differ through the feasible set that the worst-case constraint restricts and not through the ranking of designs feasible under both constraints.

claims.authorized_tex: Re-evaluating every recorded design under alternative uniform cusp priors with upper bounds \MdoPriorUppers{} and the same frozen sample rows, the robust nondominated design set restricted to the designs feasible under both the alternative and the campaign prior was identical to the campaign set for \MdoInvarianceIdenticalCount{} of \MdoPriorCount{} priors (\MdoInvarianceExactCount{} in exact arithmetic; predeclared design-set invariance \MdoInvariancePassed), while the feasible set itself moved from \MdoPriorFeasibleMin{} to \MdoPriorFeasibleMax{} designs and the unrestricted fronts from \MdoPriorFrontMin{} to \MdoPriorFrontMax{} designs (Jaccard index with the campaign front as low as \MdoPriorJaccardMin). At fixed cusp probabilities the \MdoRobustFront{} robust-Pareto designs respond as the closure dictates: the scenario \texttt{\MdoScenarioJeffreysId}, which sets the per-cell probabilities to the Jeffreys estimates of the wall-loss campaign's per-cell wall-hit counts (\MdoJeffreysCellOne, \MdoJeffreysCellTwo, \MdoJeffreysCellThree{} and \MdoJeffreysCellFour), gives a survival of \MdoScenarioJeffreysSurvival{} and a maximum thrust of \MdoScenarioJeffreysThrustMax{}~N, that is no beam, so the collisionless wall-hit probability of that campaign cannot be the per-cusp loss probability of a sustained discharge in the cusp cascade; the scenario \texttt{\MdoScenarioNoWallLossId} (survival \MdoScenarioNoWallLossSurvival, outside the sampled support whose largest survival is \MdoSampledSurvivalMax) makes \MdoScenarioNoWallLossInfeasible{} of the \MdoRobustFront{} robust-Pareto designs violate the anode-current constraint, because the worst case over a finite sample is the worst sampled case and not the worst case over the prior's support. The frozen protocol also discloses that the corrected four-cell discharge solver closed only for zero cusp probabilities in a probe of \MdoProbeTotalCases{} cases (\MdoProbeClosedCases{} converged; residual floors from \MdoProbeResidualMin{} to \MdoProbeResidualMax{} for every nonzero probability, about \MdoProbeSecondsPerSolve{}~s per multistart solve), which is why the campaign evaluates the declared closure and not that solver.

claims.authorized_tex: This campaign is optimiser evidence about the operating-point model under the declared closure \texttt{\MdoClosureId} and the declared priors, classified \texttt{\MdoClassification}: it makes no thruster-performance, plasma or physical-device claim, none of its fronts is a design recommendation, calibration or validation, and every number is conditional on that closure and on those priors. It supports no statement that any optimiser is better beyond the recorded budget of \MdoEvaluationsPerRun{} evaluations, the \MdoSeedCount{} seeds and this model. The \MdoExcludedVariableCount{} legacy geometry variables are excluded because no geometry-to-model map survives the audit, so the campaign says nothing about geometry. It is not a physics level: it consumes the accepted operating-point model with a declared closure, opens none of the field-resolved, coupled or experimental gates, and leaves the benchmark field of the committed campaign policy null.

claims.authorized_tex: Four readings follow from the admitted optimisation campaign and are bounded to its model and closure. First, constrained qLogNEHVI reached the \MdoDenseCount-design dense-reference robust hypervolume with \MdoEvaluationsPerRun{} evaluations per run (\MdoAttainedBoMin{} to \MdoAttainedBoMax{} of the reference), a statement about the optimiser on this model at this budget and these seeds, not about any thruster. Second, the robust front is materially more conservative than the nominal one: the nominal front reaches an efficiency of \MdoNominalEffMaxTwo{} and a specific impulse of \MdoNominalIspMax{}~s against \MdoRobustEffMax{} and \MdoRobustIspMax{}~s on the robust front, and the two share \MdoSharedDesigns{} designs, so a design chosen at the prior midpoints is not the design chosen under the worst sampled cusp losses. Third, the collisionless wall-hit probability of the wall-loss campaign and the per-cusp loss probability of the cusp cascade are different quantities: inserting the former as the latter gives a survival of \MdoScenarioJeffreysSurvival{} and no beam, whereas the legacy chain conflated them through the mirror formula. Fourth, the link from geometry to performance is open: no geometry-to-model map survives the audit, the \MdoExcludedVariableCount{} legacy radii were therefore excluded, and the corrected four-cell solver closed only at zero cusp probability in the recorded probe.
